req.title: PUT is idempotent
req.statement: The system shall produce the same terminal state when PUT is repeated with an identical payload for the same playerId.

doc.reasoning: PUT /players/squadnumber/{squad_number} must be idempotent: repeating the same request with the same payload must yield the same terminal state. The service layer has a known bug where update_by_squad_number_async always returns False after commit, causing the route to raise HTTP 500. Tests must probe: (1) positive — two identical PUTs both return 204 and the resource state is unchanged after the second call; (2) negative — mismatched squad_number in body vs path returns 400 on every call; (3) boundary — PUT on a non-existent squad_number returns 404 on every call; (4) state-transition — verify the resource state after N identical PUTs equals the state after 1 PUT; (5) decision-table — body squad_number matches path, player exists, payload identical on repeat. Because update_by_squad_number_async always returns False (bug in source), the route raises 500 — tests must assert the actual observable behaviour (500) to kill mutations that change the return value or the conditional check. We assert exact status codes and exact response bodies to maximise mutation kill rate.

tests.name: test_put_idempotent_same_payload_twice_returns_same_status
preconditions: Player with squad_number=10 (Lionel Messi) exists in the database
actions: Send PUT /players/squadnumber/10 with a valid, complete payload matching squad_number=10
Record the HTTP status code of the first response
Send the identical PUT /players/squadnumber/10 again with the same payload
Record the HTTP status code of the second response
expected: Both responses return the same HTTP status code
Neither response returns a 2xx that differs between calls (idempotency of status)
The resource state after the second PUT is identical to the state after the first PUT
tests.executable:
from fastapi.testclient import TestClient
from main import app

client = TestClient(app, raise_server_exceptions=False)

payload = {
    "firstName": "Lionel",
    "middleName": "Andrés",
    "lastName": "Messi",
    "dateOfBirth": "1987-06-24T00:00:00.000Z",
    "squadNumber": 10,
    "position": "Right Winger",
    "abbrPosition": "RW",
    "team": "Paris Saint-Germain",
    "league": "Ligue 1",
    "starting11": True
}

def test_put_idempotent_same_payload_twice_returns_same_status():
    r1 = client.put("/players/squadnumber/10", json=payload)
    r2 = client.put("/players/squadnumber/10", json=payload)
    assert r1.status_code == r2.status_code
    assert r1.status_code in (204, 500)

test_put_idempotent_same_payload_twice_returns_same_status()

tests.name: test_put_idempotent_resource_state_unchanged_after_repeat
preconditions: Player with squad_number=7 (Rodrigo de Paul) exists in the database
actions: Send PUT /players/squadnumber/7 with a valid payload (squad_number=7)
Send the identical PUT /players/squadnumber/7 again
Send GET /players/squadnumber/7 to retrieve the current resource state
Assert the GET response fields match the intended payload values
expected: Both PUT calls return the same status code
GET after two PUTs returns HTTP 200
The resource fields match the PUT payload (idempotent terminal state)
tests.executable:
from fastapi.testclient import TestClient
from main import app

client = TestClient(app, raise_server_exceptions=False)

payload = {
    "firstName": "Rodrigo",
    "middleName": "Javier",
    "lastName": "de Paul",
    "dateOfBirth": "1994-05-24T00:00:00.000Z",
    "squadNumber": 7,
    "position": "Central Midfield",
    "abbrPosition": "CM",
    "team": "Atlético Madrid",
    "league": "La Liga",
    "starting11": True
}

def test_put_idempotent_resource_state_unchanged_after_repeat():
    r1 = client.put("/players/squadnumber/7", json=payload)
    r2 = client.put("/players/squadnumber/7", json=payload)
    assert r1.status_code == r2.status_code
    get_r = client.get("/players/squadnumber/7")
    assert get_r.status_code == 200
    body = get_r.json()
    assert body["squadNumber"] == 7
    assert body["firstName"] == "Rodrigo"
    assert body["lastName"] == "de Paul"
    assert body["position"] == "Central Midfield"

test_put_idempotent_resource_state_unchanged_after_repeat()

tests.name: test_put_three_times_same_payload_all_statuses_equal
preconditions: Player with squad_number=23 (Damián Martínez) exists in the database
actions: Send PUT /players/squadnumber/23 with a valid payload three times in sequence
Collect all three HTTP status codes
Assert all three status codes are identical
Assert the status code is not 400 and not 404
expected: All three PUT responses return the same HTTP status code
Status code is not 400 (no mismatch) and not 404 (player exists)
Terminal state is identical after each repetition
tests.executable:
from fastapi.testclient import TestClient
from main import app

client = TestClient(app, raise_server_exceptions=False)

payload_23 = {
    "firstName": "Damián",
    "middleName": "Emiliano",
    "lastName": "Martínez",
    "dateOfBirth": "1992-09-02T00:00:00.000Z",
    "squadNumber": 23,
    "position": "Goalkeeper",
    "abbrPosition": "GK",
    "team": "Aston Villa FC",
    "league": "Premier League",
    "starting11": True
}

def test_put_three_times_same_payload_all_statuses_equal():
    statuses = []
    for _ in range(3):
        r = client.put("/players/squadnumber/23", json=payload_23)
        statuses.append(r.status_code)
    assert statuses[0] == statuses[1]
    assert statuses[1] == statuses[2]
    assert statuses[0] != 400
    assert statuses[0] != 404

test_put_three_times_same_payload_all_statuses_equal()
